judge: designer (figures for magazine articles and mathematics textbooks)
scale: 1-10, higher is better; for clutter, higher means less clutter
evidence: every PNG in directions/A|B|C and before/ (8 scenes; plane light/dark t=0.5, t=1, playing, globe, Article B/W, Homework B/W, globe Article B/W, Article colour)

live in the work copy (headless Chrome, 1440x900, window.__pathStyle = A|B|C): jouk, chain3, mobius, cosstrip scrubbed to t = 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 of the range and two frames while playing; 60 fps while playing for all 12 (p95 17-17.5 ms); no exceptions; the same points at every t in all three

A: Live it is the calmest of the three, and a frame taken while playing looks like a still: only the heads, then trails that grow. Best in motion.
Static, the tapered trails read as pins or tadpoles. The direction needs the 'thick = late' convention, and the gradient-comet look is the one most likely to read as generic.
Print is weak: the six-grey tails fade into the 50 % checker (jouk Article), and in chain3 and cosstrip the long loops still cross through the image.
Point choice: jouk's far field still dominates (needles from the frame edge), and the cusp loop is still there.
B: The Article figures are the most article-grade: jouk, chain3's outer arcs, mobius and cos read like textbook flow plots, and small arrowheads give the direction everywhere.
Too many paths: jouk shows 44 radial needles live and in print (a pincushion, still chaotic at a glance).
'Never crosses' fails at sinks: a starburst at 0 in chain3, and nested small arcs crammed against mobius's sink.
Live: the faint full-length rails plus arrowheads ahead of the head make it the busiest of the three, and while playing the rails give away the future.
The white casing still reads as a railroad (a double line) on the grey checker.
The globe export reads as hatching (mobius: about 20 parallel diagonal lines with arrows).
C: Tells the right story where the boundary is the point: the real line wrapping onto the circle (mobius), the circle collapsing onto the airfoil (jouk), chain3's bottom edge as nested arcs. This is the cleanest live frame of the four I scrubbed.
Beads at t = 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 are a refined, print-safe way to show speed and direction with no gradients and no arrowhead pile-ups.
Too sparse when the boundary is small: the jouk export is a nearly empty checker with 4 paths, and the far field and interior are never shown.
Boundary paths cross each other freely: string-art in cosstrip and in chain3's lower left.
The open-ring to filled-dot convention needs its caption.

winner_reason: C has the higher total, but I would not ship it alone: showing only the boundary is a narrow view and empties the general case (jouk). B's placement (evenly spaced, Jobard-Lefer) is the structural fix the user's complaint ('chaotic') calls for, and its export is closest to an article figure. B is the base; its live view and density need the grafts below.
graft: From A: the live and playing view draws only the travelled part 0..t with a head dot. Drop B's faint rails ahead of the head and the arrowheads while playing, so motion frames look like rest frames.

From C: time beads at t = 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 (with a filled end dot) in place of B's arrowheads every 30 pt in print. Keep at most one arrowhead per path, near the end. Beads show speed and direction and never pile up.
From C: seed B's streamlines from the boundary of X first (boundary seeds at the spacing, then interior seeds fill the gaps), so the boundary story is always present and jouk's airfoil gets paths.
Halve B's density: separation about 1.5x today's 0.6x16 px, cap about 20-24 on a desktop pane and about 12 in the Article. 44 is a pincushion.

Fix B's sinks: end a path when it enters a ring around a shared sink or within the separation of a kept path near its end, instead of letting every path reach the sink (chain3's starburst at 0, mobius's crammed arcs).
From A: the farthest-point spread of heads (end points at least 26 px apart), as a second test on B's choice, so heads never cluster where the map contracts.
Print casing: replace the 1.3 pt white casing with a thin casing (about 0.3-0.4 pt) in the plane's paper colour, or none over the light squares, to end the railroad double line on the grey checker.
Globe: space on the sphere and cap at about 8-10 paths, and never draw a family of parallels (B's mobius globe export reads as hatching). C's boundary paths are the right default on the globe.
Captions per style: 'dot z, beads at t = 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, filled dot F(z)'.
